paper.title: Disagreement-Based Combinatorial Pure Exploration: Sample Complexity Bounds and an Efficient Algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration, fixed confidence setting
unmapped: Goal: identify the subset v in a known decision set V maximizing sum of arm means, querying one base arm per step and observing its sample
Learner knows the decision set V and its combinatorial parameters Phi and Psi
Fixed confidence: delta given as input, must output v* with prob >= 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: we are given a finite set of arms $A \triangleq \{1,\ldots, K\}$, where arm $a$ is associated with a sub-Gaussian distribution $\nu_a$ with unknown mean $\mu_a \in [-1,1]$ and variance parameter $1$. Further, we are given a decision set $\Vcal \subseteq 2^A$. ... In the fixed confidence setting, a failure probability parameter $\delta$ is provided as input to the algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration, fixed budget setting
unmapped: Goal: identify the best subset v in a known decision set V (sum of arm means), querying one base arm per step
Learner knows the decision set V
settings.definition_quote: In the fixed budget setting, the learning algorithm is given a budget of $T$ queries, after which it must produce an estimate $\hat{v}$ of the true optimum $v^\star$, and we seek to minimize the probability of error $\PP[\hat{v} \ne v^\star]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration, non-interactive (uniform sampling) setting
unmapped: Best subset identification in known decision set V
Non-interactive: each arm queried T/K times uniformly
settings.definition_quote: With budget $T$, a non-interactive algorithm queries each arm $T/K$ times and then outputs an estimate $\hat{v}$ of $v^\star$.

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration, non-interactive setting (lower bound)
unmapped: Best subset identification in known decision set V
Non-interactive: each arm queried T/K times
settings.definition_quote: any non-interactive algorithm must have $\sup_{v^\star \in \Vcal} \sup_{\mu \in \Scal(v^\star,\Delta)} \PP_{\mu}[\hat{v} \ne v^\star] \ge 1/2$

algorithms.name: Fixed Confidence Algorithm (Algorithm 1, disagreement-based with oracle-based Disagree via FTPL)

symbols.Delta_v_min: min over v != v* of normalized gap <v*-v,mu>/d(v*,v)
symbols.Phi: max_{k,v} log|B(k,v)|/k, growth rate of decision set
symbols.Psi: minimum symmetric difference between distinct sets in V

source.label: thm:noninteractive_upper
source.quote: For any $\mu \in [-1,1]^K$ and $\delta \in (0,1)$ the non-interactive MLE guarantees $\PP_{\mu}[\hat{v}\ne v^\star] \le \delta$ with $T = \order\left(\frac{K}{\min_{v\ne v^\star} \Delta_v^2}\left(\Phi + \frac{\log(K/\delta)}{\Psi}\right)\right)$.

results.notes: Budget T sufficient for error <= delta. MLE needs a linear optimization oracle.

symbols.Phi: max_{k,v} log|B(k,v)|/k, growth rate of decision set
symbols.Delta: lower bound on all normalized gaps Delta_v(mu) in the class S(v*,Delta)

conditions: any non-interactive algorithm (each arm sampled T/K times)
worst case over v* in V and mu in S(v*,Delta)
hard instances are homogeneous Gaussian mu = Delta(2v-1)
worst-case error probability >= 1/2 whenever T is below the bound

source.label: thm:noninteractive_upper
source.quote: any non-interactive algorithm must have $\sup_{v^\star \in \Vcal} \sup_{\mu \in \Scal(v^\star,\Delta)} \PP_{\mu}[\hat{v} \ne v^\star] \ge 1/2$ as long as $T \le \frac{K}{ \Delta^2}\left(\Phi - \log \log 3\right)$.

results.notes: Stated as error >= 1/2 if T below threshold; recorded as a sample-complexity lower bound for constant confidence. Fano-based (minimax construction).

symbols.Delta_a: arm gap min_{v: a in v* sym-diff v} <v*-v,mu>/d(v*,v)
symbols.Psi: minimum symmetric difference between distinct sets in V

tuning: Delta_t = min{1, sqrt(8/t (Phi Psi + log(K pi^2 t^2/delta))/Psi)}

source.label: thm:fixconsc
source.quote: For any combinatorial exploration instance with mean vector $\mu$, and any $\delta \in (0,1)$,~\pref{alg:main} guarantees that $\PP[\hat{v} \ne v^\star] \le \delta$. Moreover, it runs in polynomial time with access to the optimization oracle, and the total number of samples is at most \sum_{a \in K}\frac{144}{\Delta_a^2}\left(\Phi + \frac{2\log(144/(\Delta_a^2\Psi)) + 2\log(K\pi^2/\delta)}{\Psi}\right).

results.notes: Polynomial time given linear optimization oracle (oracle-efficient). Sample bound holds on the 1-delta event.

symbols.Psi: minimum symmetric difference between distinct sets in V
symbols.H_tilde: max_j (K+1-j) (Delta^{(j)})^{-2}, Delta^{(j)} the j-th largest arm gap Delta_a

source.label: thm:fixed_budget
source.quote: Given budget $T\ge K$, there exists a fixed budget algorithm (\pref{alg:fixbudget} in~\pref{app:fixed_budget}) that guarantees \PP[\hat{v} \ne v] \le K^2 \exp \left\{\Psi \left(\Phi -  \frac{(T-K)}{9\tlog(K) \tilde{H}}\right)  \right\}.

results.notes: Algorithm not oracle-efficient (paper says so); compute not stated as polynomial.

symbols.H1_a: max_{v: a in v sym-diff v*} d(v,v*)/<mu,v*-v>^2
symbols.H2_a: max_{v: a in v sym-diff v*} d(v,v*) D(v,v*)/<mu,v*-v>^2, D symmetric log-volume

conditions: sub-Gaussian (Gaussian in pseudocode) noise with unit variance

source.label: thm:refinefixcon
source.quote: There exists a fixed confidence algorithm (\pref{alg:inefffixcon} in~\pref{app:refined_proof}) that guarantees $\PP[\hat{v} \ne v^\star] \le \delta$ with sample complexity T \le 64 \sum_{a\in[K]} H^{(1)}_{a} \left( 2\log(64H^{(1)}_{a}) + \log\frac{\pi^2 K}{\delta}\right) + 64 H^{(2)}_a.

results.notes: As printed, 64 H^{(2)}_a appears outside the sum (typo); proof shows per-arm term, so recorded inside the sum. Algorithm is computationally inefficient (explicit enumeration of V).
